rationale: Round 1 built and ran cleanly with no ICE fallback, so this candidate shifts from a conservative baseline toward materially higher reverse-engineering resistance while keeping overhead bounded. SUB is pushed hardest (0.8 security) because the profile is dominated by small arithmetic-heavy functions (five11, main, read_11_bits) where instruction substitution is nearly free and directly obscures the bit-manipulation logic that is this benchmark's core. ICALL and IGV are raised (0.7 security / 0.7 diversity) since indirect-call conversion and global-variable flattening add strong static-analysis friction at low runtime and size cost, suiting a 1259-byte text footprint where size budget is tight. SPLIT stays a diversity workhorse for breaking up the two ~360-byte functions. BCF, FLA, and IBR get elevated security weights (0.7) but their RuntimeCost weights stay at 0.4 rather than higher: the program is a timing-sensitive MultiSource benchmark whose hot paths (read_x_bits, the five11 decode loop) would suffer from aggressive bogus-control-flow and flattening, so the mid weight lets the feature-driven selector apply them where features favor it while sparing the hottest loops. CorrectnessRisk stays low across the board (0.1-0.2) because round 1 showed the toolchain handles these passes on this target, leaving headroom without endangering the verified-correct baseline.
